sections.h2: What is different about a Rochester Hills sale?
sections.html:
Rochester Hills is a high-value Oakland County suburb, yet the paperwork is modest: a deed filed with the county, two affidavits for the city's Assessing Department, and a treasurer's tax certificate. Most of the work happens at the county and state level.

Downtown Detroit is roughly 25 miles south. European settlement began in 1817, Avon Township was organized in 1835, and a 1984 charter vote turned the township into the City of Rochester Hills. The older city of Rochester incorporated in 1967 and remains a separate municipality, a distinction buyers often blur.

sections.h2: How did Rochester Hills become a city?
sections.html:
Rochester Hills incorporated late and after a long fight over its boundaries. The Potawatomi lived along the Clinton River and Paint Creek until the 1807 Treaty of Detroit ceded southeast Michigan, and the township that followed adopted a charter in 1948 under the Home Rule Act. A post office called Brooklands opened that same year between Auburn Road and Hamlin Road.

After Rochester became its own city in 1967, its residents stopped paying township property tax. Three proposed city charters failed between 1969 and 1971, and a dispute over a 1974 annexation by Rochester stayed in the courts until 1981. In May 1984 township voters approved a charter, and the new city took the name Rochester Hills over the alternative Avon Hills. When the title company asks for a legal description, match it to the parcel number on your tax bill.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Rochester Hills households?
sections.html:
The land area is 32.80 square miles, about 2,326 residents live on each, and the July 2025 estimate of 77,539 sits 1.6 percent above the 76,321 counted at the 2020 base.

Two lines stand out. Roughly three homes in four are lived in by their owners, which leaves little rental stock competing with your listing. Also, 23.6 percent of residents use another language at home, so consider translated listing details and flexible showing plans.

sections.h2: Which schools serve Rochester Hills addresses?
sections.html:
Rochester Community Schools serve most of the city, with Rochester Adams High School, Rochester High School and Stoney Creek High School all inside the city limits. Part of Rochester Hills falls in the Avondale School District instead, where many addresses are zoned to Deer Field Elementary in the city, while others go to Auburn Elementary in Auburn Hills or Woodland Elementary in Troy.

All Avondale residents attend Avondale Middle School in Rochester Hills and Avondale High School in Auburn Hills. Addresses in different parts of the city can belong to different districts, so get an official boundary check before a listing names a school.

Colleges add a buyer group: Oakland University and Rochester Christian University both offer programs here. The city runs the Rochester Hills Public Library and, by contract, lets residents of the city of Rochester and Oakland Township use it.

Rochester Hills is rolling, as the name suggests. Elevation climbs from about 690 feet in the southeast to 1,032 feet in the northwest, and the Clinton River and Paint Creek were the water sources that drew the first settlers.

Its boundaries run as follows:

  • Oakland Charter Township to the north, along Dutton Road.
  • Troy to the south, along South Boulevard.
  • Shelby Township in Macomb County to the east, along Dequindre Road, with the city of Rochester partly on the eastern edge.
  • Auburn Hills to the west, along part of Adams Road.

The city keeps no police department of its own, and the Oakland County Sheriff's Office provides police service. The 52nd District Court's third division sits in the city too. When a buyer asks about services, send them to the city's website and the sheriff's office.

sections.h2: Which forms go to Rochester Hills assessing after closing?
sections.html:
Two documents go to the Assessing Department at 1000 Rochester Hills Drive: a Property Transfer Affidavit and, for an owner-occupant, a Principal Residence Exemption affidavit. The city expects the closing agent to give the buyer both, and they can be mailed or dropped off during weekday office hours.

The exemption lifts up to 18 mills of school tax off a bill when the owner lives there as a main residence. Sellers should ask Assessing for the rescission form so the exemption on the old home ends cleanly. The department also administers disabled veteran and poverty exemptions, and the poverty request has to be refiled every year.

A buyer who wants a quick tax estimate can follow the city's rule of thumb, which halves the estimated value and applies the current millage rate, or ask Assessing to run it. An owner who disputes a value gets one chance a year: the March Board of Review, after the February notice.

sections.h2: What does the Oakland County deed filing involve?
sections.html:
A deed filed with the Oakland County Register of Deeds costs $30, which already contains the state's $4 survey surcharge. A discharge or assignment that cites several earlier recordings adds $3 for each extra reference, and copies run $1 a page.

The county treasurer must certify warranty deeds and land contracts first, for $5. When you mail the deed, the Register of Deeds can obtain that certificate if your payment includes the extra $5. Expect about two weeks to get a hand-delivered document back and two to four weeks by mail.

The county's fee page states both transfer tax shares: $0.55 per $500 for the county and $3.75 per $500 for the state. A deed with consideration under $100 is exempt, and any other claimed exemption must appear on the deed. The seller carries the bill under MCL 207.523.

sections.h2: What does the Rochester Hills tax calendar mean for my closing?
sections.html:
The summer bill covers school and county levies only. It is payable July 1 through September 14, and 1 percent interest starts September 15. Winter bills open December 1 and fall due in mid-February.

  • The city shows February 16, 2027 as the winter due date for the 2026 tax year, with a 3 percent penalty shortly after.
  • Anything still owed turns delinquent on March 2 and moves to the Oakland County Treasurer.
  • Postmarks do not count, so pay in person or online close to a deadline.
  • E-check payments are free online, while cards and mobile wallets add a 2.75 percent processing charge.

The winter bill adds the city's own levy for police and fire services, roads and the library, so a fall or winter closing can land before it is paid. Have the title company say who pays it and how it is credited, and use the Treasury tax look-up to see each parcel's status.

faqs.q: Where is a Rochester Hills deed recorded?
faqs.a: At the Oakland County Register of Deeds, for $30 including the $4 survey surcharge. Warranty deeds first need a $5 treasurer certificate.

faqs.q: Must a Rochester Hills house pass a city inspection before closing?
faqs.a: Ask the city's Building Department whether one applies to your address, and do it before you pick a closing date. The Assessing Department only handles tax forms.

faqs.q: What paperwork does a Rochester Hills buyer owe the city?
faqs.a: A Property Transfer Affidavit, and an exemption affidavit for a buyer who will live there. Both go to Assessing at 1000 Rochester Hills Drive.

faqs.q: What are the tax deadlines in Rochester Hills?
faqs.a: September 14 for summer and mid-February for winter, listed as February 16, 2027 for the 2026 bill. Oakland County takes over unpaid balances on March 2.

faqs.q: Who covers transfer tax on a Rochester Hills sale?
faqs.a: The seller. The county lists $3.75 per $500 for the state portion and $0.55 per $500 for its own.
